previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy and PEG dependence, and a history of osteonecrosis was readmitted for tachypnea and coffee-ground emesis. He had recently been discharged after treatment for pseudomonal UTI. Evaluation revealed leukocytosis and elevated lactate, with concern for aspiration pneumonitis due to inappropriate oral intake at rehab. Chest imaging showed chronic interstitial lung disease without new consolidation. He improved with supportive care, including suctioning and nebulizers, and did not require antibiotic escalation despite Pseudomonas growth in sputum. A brief SVT episode resolved with vagal maneuvers. Trazodone was discontinued after contributing to altered mental status. Pain from chronic osteonecrosis was managed with acetaminophen. He stabilized, completed treatment, and was discharged back to rehabilitation with updated orders for NPO status and medication adjustments.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ and Dr.
___ radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
___ supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure
and has reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: Sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of 0 mcg of
fentanyl and 2 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service time of 23
minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine was injected
in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS:  Lidocaine jelly.
CONTRAST: 25 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  12.42 min, 123 mGy

PROCEDURE:  1. Replacement of a ___ low profile 3.5 cm stomal length MIC
gastrojejunostomy tube.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table.  A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The tube site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.
A scout image of the abdomen was obtained.  This showed that the existing
gastrojejunostomy tube was partially coiled in the stomach.  A stiff glide
wire was advanced through the existing tube, but this exacerbated the loop in
the stomach.  Therefore, a Glidewire was advanced over a Kumpe catheter
alongside the existing tube through the same hole into the stomach.  The wire
was removed a contrast injection was performed to confirm positioning within
the stomach.  Over a 6 ___ sheath, the Glidewire and Kumpe catheter were
directed into the jejunum.  The wire was removed and a contrast injection was
performed to confirm positioning.  Then the Glidewire was exchanged for a
stiff Glidewire over the Kumpe catheter.  The Kumpe catheter and sheath were
then removed.  A new 18 ___ MIC gastrojejunostomy tube was then advanced
over the stiff Glidewire, after removing the existing gastrojejunostomy tube. 
The balloon was inflated.  A contrast injection was performed to confirm
positioning.  The tube was then flushed.
The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1. Successful replacement of a 18 ___ MIC gastrojejunostomy tube, low
profile with 3.5 cm stomal length with its tip in the proximal jejunum.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a 18 ___ MIC gastrojejunostomy tube, low profile
with 3.5 cm stomal length, with its tip in the proximal jejunum. The tube is
ready for use.

EXAMINATION:  CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with hx of hiv/aids, recurrent UTI.  eval for
structural GU abnormality or stone  // eval for structural GU abnormality or
stone

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 8.5 s, 55.4 cm; CTDIvol = 3.2 mGy (Body) DLP = 174.4
mGy-cm.
   2) Sequenced Acquisition 0.5 s, 0.2 cm; CTDIvol = 7.3 mGy (Body) DLP = 1.5
mGy-cm.
   3) Stationary Acquisition 20.7 s, 0.2 cm; CTDIvol = 276.6 mGy (Body) DLP =
55.3 mGy-cm.
   4) Spiral Acquisition 8.1 s, 52.9 cm; CTDIvol = 5.7 mGy (Body) DLP = 297.8
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 529 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made with CT abdomen and pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Severe interstitial lung disease is seen in the lung bases
bilaterally, similar to prior exam.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic
or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder multiple gallstones and
sludge without evidence of acute cholecystitis.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable.  A GJ-tube has been pulled back
somewhat and now terminates in the second or third part of the duodenum. 
Bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement
throughout.  A bowel anastomosis is noted in the right lower quadrant.

PELVIS:  There is a 6 mm stone in the right UVJ.  There is no associated
hydroureter or hydronephrosis.  The bladder demonstrates a thickened and
irregular wall, suggestive of cystitis.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The reproductive organs are unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture. 
Compression deformity is noted in T11, similar to prior exam.  Orthopedic
hardware is noted in the proximal femurs bilaterally.  There is diffuse
osteopenia.

SOFT TISSUES: The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  6 mm stone in the right UVJ without associated hydroureter or
hydronephrosis.

2. Bladder demonstrates a thickened and irregular wall, suggestive of
cystitis.

3.  GJ-tube has been pulled back somewhat and now terminates in the second or
third part of the duodenum.

4. Cholelithiasis without evidence of acute cholecystitis.

5.  Severe interstitial lung disease, similar to prior exam.
